facts.text: Lewisham’s clock tower, completed in 1900, was built to commemorate Queen Victoria’s Diamond Jubilee.
The 1887 Battle of Lewisham saw local residents defend the town against a mob, a rare civil‑defence episode in London.
Goldsmiths College, founded as a technical institute in 1891, now belongs to the University of London and sits just outside Lewisham in New Cross.
Lewisham’s archives hold more than five centuries of history, with records dating back to 1476, available in the reading room at Catford Library.
Ginger Baker, the legendary drummer who co‑founded Cream, was born and raised in Lewisham, adding rock heritage to the borough.
The former roundabout by Lewisham station was replaced with an “H” junction in the 1990s, freeing land for private development.
